title: Sam Altman Warns AI Race With China Can’t Justify ‘Recklessness’—‘No Reason Any of Us Should Come to Work’ Without Safety Accountability

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said late Sunday that artificial intelligence (AI) labs owe the world confidence that they will develop increasingly capable systems responsibly and that the cost of building in safety is worth paying no matter how intense the competitive pressure gets.

Every frontier lab has to deliver on responsible development, Altman argued in a post on X, or there's "no reason any of us should come to work."

  • Still Learning the Market? These 50 Must-Know Terms Can Help You Catch Up Fast

OpenAI has also been using "safety cases" and monitoring as part of its approach to managing increasingly capable models, while Altman said companies should not wait for legislation to begin implementing safeguards.

"When we talk about "pacing", we do not mean "stopping". Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs."

The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We…

— Sam Altman (@sama) September 14, 2026

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

OpenAI Waits, Anthropic Moves Ahead on IPO Plans

His comments follow OpenAI's decision to rule out a 2026 IPO, calling it "an ill-advised moment to go public."

Anthropic, on the other hand, is reportedly moving ahead with its own listing, targeting a $2 trillion valuation on the Nasdaq as early as October.

Altman warned that "no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring."

A Split Among Industry Leaders

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend essay warned that a swarm of rogue AI agents could seize control of parts of the internet within six to 12 months, urging an industry-wide slowdown.

He called China the "toughest dilemma" in any push for a global slowdown, warning that racing ahead creates powerful incentives to keep accelerating.
